Senses.Note: Not a single thing is a complete negative quantity phrase. The retained records put it in an encomium, answers about livelihood or what is present, and Mazu's rebuke; the surrounding predicates must not be silently imported into the phrase.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X81/X81n1568.xml). Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps (Vols. 10–25) (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)). Speaker: the Lingquan monastery master.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X80/X80n1565.xml). Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元). Speaker: Mazu Daoyi.

Senses.Explanation: Not a single thing denies that even one object or possession is present in the locally stated domain. Jifei Ruyi's encomium on Huineng invokes the absence of a single thing before mentioning the waist stone. The unlinked Lingquan master answers a question about his livelihood with the phrase, then responds to a question about daily use. Tianyin Xiu answers an unidentified monastic asking what he has with the same phrase, then says that questioner still has something. Mazu Daoyi tells Dazhu Huihai that there is not a single thing at his place and redirects him to his own treasure. The domains differ, but the negative quantity remains stable.
